title: 7th Sitting of third session of 2026
presiding: Deputy Speaker Ahmed Saleem (until the 10:28 break); Speaker Abdul Raheem Abdulla after the break
summary: Members continued debating a public petition, sent by the Petitions Committee, asking to end the health insurance MPs receive that ordinary citizens do not; most speakers argued the petition was misleading or that the benefit is set by law and the Constitution, while some said the wider health system should be fixed. The debate closed when PNC time ran out. Three government tax bills (income tax, GST and tax administration amendments) got their first reading, and the preliminary debate on a government bill setting privileges for diplomatic missions, consular posts and international organisations was held and closed, with the vote set for voting time. The Speaker then took the chair and the Finance Committee report on the Auditor General's Office 2027 budget was presented and debate began; this part ends mid-debate. Parts of the text layer are jumbled, so some details are approximate. This part closes the debate on the Public Accounts (Finance) Committee report on the Auditor General's Office 2027 budget. One member, continuing from part 1, called for the office to be strengthened and politically neutral; the Kendhoo member said the budget had been cut well below what the office requested and asked for it to be restored at the budget stage. The House then voted 43-0 to accept the bill on privileges and immunities of diplomatic missions, consular posts and international organisations (sent to the Foreign Relations Committee), and 46-0 to approve the Auditor General's Office 2027 budget of about MVR 133.59 million.

items.title: Finance Committee report on the Auditor General's Office budget for 2027

speakers.name: Hassan Mufeed Abdul Gadir
positions: Said the insurance petition misrepresents facts and other countries' examples, and is aimed at creating political discord.
Supported the diplomatic privileges bill, saying it balances sovereignty with international obligations and keeps foreign diplomats bound by Maldivian law.

speakers.name: Ahmed Riyaz
positions: Said he would support cutting any benefit citizens lack, but called the petition untrue and aimed at headlines; noted MPs' insurance costs about 2,000 rufiyaa a month.

speakers.name: Saudulla Hilmy
positions: Said MP insurance costs about 2,000 rufiyaa a month and covers only treatment under set rules, but the issue deserves more thought if many citizens want change.

speakers.name: Hussain Shareef
positions: Welcomed the petition, saying MPs are servants of the people; argued the state system should give ordinary citizens fast access to care without needing an MP's help.

speakers.name: Hussain Hameed
positions: Said MP insurance is required by an earlier law, not requested by MPs, and linked the petition to past abuse of the state insurance scheme.

speakers.name: Abdul Sattar Mohamed
positions: Thanked petitioners but argued the focus should be on reforming the whole system rather than one issue.

speakers.name: Mohamed Shahid
positions: Argued MPs are portrayed as highly privileged but in practice have few protections or benefits; said the petition aims to divide MPs and the public.

speakers.name: Ahmed Nazim
positions: Said MP benefits stem from Constitution Article 102, which also covers the President, ministers, judges and independent bodies, and are not unique to MPs.

speakers.name: Mohamed Dawoodh
positions: Presented the government bill setting a legal framework for privileges of diplomatic missions, consular posts, UN agencies and international organisations in line with treaties.

speakers.name: Dr. Anara Naeem
positions: Supported the diplomatic privileges bill, noting the Maldives' long record of maintaining foreign relations under successive governments.

speakers.name: Mohamed Fazeel
positions: Called the diplomatic privileges bill important because no law currently sets the protections owed to missions and international bodies.

speakers.name: Mohamed Musthafa Ibrahim
positions: Thanked the sponsor and President Muizzu for the bill; noted the Maldives joined the 1961 Vienna Convention on Diplomatic Relations in 1966.

speakers.name: Hassan Zareer
positions: Welcomed the diplomatic privileges bill as an important step consistent with treaties the Maldives has joined.

speakers.name: Mohamed Mamdooh
positions: Presented the Finance Committee report on the Auditor General's Office 2027 budget under the Audit Act.

speakers.name: Dr. Ahmed Shamheed
positions: Said much Auditor General effort goes to costly audits of councils with small sums, and the office should focus on high-value audits.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Falah
positions: Noted the report passed committee with all parties' agreement and the 2027 budget is lower than last year; said audit findings are often not acted on.

speakers.name: Mauroof Zakir
positions: Said the Auditor General's Office budget was cut many times below its request and below last year, including staff spending
Argued the office protects taxpayer money, debt sustainability and public trust, and asked for the budget to be raised during the budget stage

decisions: Debate on the MP health insurance petition concluded after PNC's allotted time ran out
First reading given to the Income Tax Act amendment bill
First reading given to the GST Act amendment bill
First reading given to the Tax Administration Act amendment bill
Preliminary debate on the diplomatic missions privileges bill concluded; chair announced the vote at voting time

Bill on privileges and immunities of diplomatic missions, consular posts and international organisations (proposed by Kulhudhuffushi North MP Mohamed Dawood on behalf of the government) accepted and sent to the Foreign Relations Committee under rule 106(r)
Auditor General's Office 2027 budget of MVR 133,596,265 approved as recommended by the Finance Committee
Next sitting announced for Wednesday 21 October 2026 at 9:00

votes.what: Accept the diplomatic missions, consular posts and international organisations privileges and immunities bill
Approve the Auditor General's Office 2027 budget as decided by the Finance Committee
